title_en: The Doctor Who Drank Bacteria to Win an Argument
english_paragraphs: In 1984 Barry Marshall, a 32-year-old doctor at Fremantle Hospital, drank a brew of beef broth into which the microbial growth of two Petri dishes had been scraped.
The prevalent doctrine blamed ulcers on stress, spicy food, and excess acid secretion. No bacterium, the profession firmly held, could withstand so caustic and hostile a habitat.

Yet Robin Warren, a pathologist at Royal Perth Hospital, had seen curved, coiled bacteria in gastric biopsies from patients with gastritis. Marshall began to collaborate with him. Attempts to culture the germ were invariably unsuccessful until Easter 1982, when plates sat undisturbed in the incubator for about five days. They were ordinarily binned after two. Colonies blossomed. The organism was later named Helicobacter pylori.

In 1983 unimpressed assessors at the Gastroenterological Society of Australia relegated the pair's paper to the bottom tenth of that year's submissions. Efforts to infect swine were likewise in vain. Marshall made himself the guinea pig.

Within days Marshall was vomiting, his breath had a disagreeable odour and weariness set in. About ten days later an endoscopy revealed gastritis, an inflammation of the stomach's mucous membrane and a precursor to ulcers, albeit not an ulcer itself. The germ was cultured directly from his stomach.
Spurred on by his insistent spouse, Marshall took antibiotics, which cleared the infection. Ulcers came to be treated with such medication.

In 2005 Marshall and Warren shared the Nobel Prize in Physiology or Medicine for discovering Helicobacter pylori and its role in gastritis and peptic ulcer disease. Gastritis, the illness Marshall had willingly given himself, is named in the prize citation.
chinese_paragraphs: 1984年，弗里曼特尔医院32岁的医生巴里·马歇尔喝下了一份牛肉清汤混合液，里面加入了从两个培养皿中刮取的微生物培养物。
当时占主导地位的学说把溃疡归因于压力、辛辣食物和胃酸分泌过多。医学界坚信，没有细菌能够在这样具有腐蚀性、又不利于生存的环境中存活。
然而，皇家珀斯医院的病理学家罗宾·沃伦，已经在胃炎患者的胃部活检样本中看到了弯曲、盘绕的细菌。马歇尔开始与他合作。培养这种病菌的尝试一直未获成功，直到1982年复活节期间，培养皿在培养箱里原封不动地放了约五天。通常，这些培养皿两天后就会被丢弃。菌落这一次长了出来。这种微生物后来被命名为幽门螺杆菌。
1983年，澳大利亚胃肠病学会的评审者对这项研究并不看好，把两人的论文列入了当年投稿中排名最低的十分之一。让猪感染这种细菌的努力也同样没有成功。于是，马歇尔把自己当成了实验对象。
几天之内，马歇尔开始呕吐，呼出的气带有难闻的气味，身体也逐渐感到疲倦。大约十天后，胃镜检查发现他患了胃炎，也就是胃黏膜的炎症，属于溃疡的前期病变，但它本身并不是溃疡。研究者还直接从他的胃中培养出了这种病菌。
在妻子不断催促下，马歇尔服用了抗生素，感染随之被清除。后来，溃疡也逐渐开始采用这类药物治疗。
2005年，马歇尔与沃伦因发现幽门螺杆菌及其在胃炎和消化性溃疡中的作用，共同获得诺贝尔生理学或医学奖。马歇尔当年主动让自己患上的胃炎，也被写进了获奖评语。

illustration_prompt:
Create a single publication-quality landscape 3:2 narrative illustration for an adult illustrated English-reading booklet. Finished standalone artwork, not a book mockup, not a collage of multiple unrelated panels. Sophisticated contemporary editorial gouache and watercolor, carefully controlled colored-pencil accents, velvety matte paint, subtle warm paper texture, soft natural daylight. Warm ivory paper dominates; subdued eucalyptus and sage greens structure the composition; restrained buttery lemon-yellow and dusty terracotta accents. Calm, comfortable, refined, credible drawing and natural anatomy. An airy coherent composition with one clear story focal point and at most two supporting details, generous breathing room at all edges and softly feathered painted edges into ivory. Detailed but uncluttered. Historically and scientifically appropriate objects, clothing and setting. Show the particular article's pivotal event or mechanism rather than a generic portrait or generic textbook symbols. Human figures treated with dignity; no grotesque caricature, no sensational violence or visible injuries. For disasters, emphasize the setting, evidence or human response without graphic suffering. For uncertain scientific claims, depict the observations and investigation without presenting debated mechanisms as proven. Absolutely no typography, captions, letters, numbers, logos, watermarks, diagram labels, fake writing or invented charts anywhere. Do not render invisible forces as literal magic. Avoid corporate vector icons, slick 3D rendering and childish cartoon style. High-quality, print-ready visual storytelling, matching a warm ivory-and-sage adult watercolor booklet.

ARTICLE 03 — The Doctor Who Drank Bacteria to Win an Argument. Depict the pivotal successful bacterial culture in an early-1980s Australian hospital laboratory: two adult male medical researchers, one in his early thirties and one middle-aged, calmly collaborating over a small clear Petri dish with a few tiny bacterial colonies. The younger researcher carefully holds the dish at bench height, the older one observes closely; natural faces and anatomically credible hands. Their plain white laboratory coats have no badges or text. A simple closed laboratory incubator and a small covered flask of pale beef broth are the only supporting objects, in the background rather than competing focal points. A warm ivory bench and diffuse daylight, sage-green shadows, restrained terracotta and lemon accents. Treat the researchers with dignity. Show culture and evidence, not a stomach ulcer, not miraculous healing, not a triumphant debate, and not an instruction for drinking bacteria. Avoid giant floating microbes, glowing particles, modern DNA screens, paperwork, labels, numerals or any lettering. One airy coherent landscape 3:2 scene with softly painted edges into ivory.

马歇尔喝下菌液后患的是胃炎，并非溃疡；胃中也培养出了同种细菌。
